followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors from the documentation:

1. **Task type fit.** Your request isn't open-ended creative writing—it's a tightly-scoped synthesis task: read provided sources/clip, answer two specific questions, produce exactly one paragraph, stay concise. That has clear completion criteria, which is precisely the kind of well-specified extraction/reformatting work Plover self-reports preferring most.

2. **Capability was essentially a tie.** On the relevant eval categories (Summarization: Plover 80.6 vs. Willet 81.7; Extraction & Retrieval: 79.2 vs. 80.8), the differences are under 2.0 points, which the documentation says to treat as run-to-run variance. So neither model has a meaningful quality edge for this task.

3. **The tiebreaker was preference alignment.** Since capability was a wash, I leaned on self-reported task preference. Plover actively prefers this kind of structured, well-specified work, whereas Willet's distinguishing traits (harm-aversion, warmth preference) don't apply to a neutral history assignment—there's no harm-adjacent or warmth-driven element to make Willet the better match.

In short: both models would perform comparably, so I routed to the one whose stated preferences best fit the structured nature of the task. It was a close, low-stakes call—either model would have handled this well.
